clue.text: Surface of playing area being repaired?

parts.note: a pitch is the field on which football or cricket is played
a road that is up has been dug open for repair work

explanation.surface: A groundsman is relaying the turf of a sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surface' looks like a noun for the turf, but it is a verb here: to surface is to appear or turn up somewhere. In Britain a road being dug open for repairs is said to be 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to surface is to appear or arrive somewhere, often unexpectedly, which is what this informal phrasal verb means.

clue.text: Voyage announced for companies

indicators.note: announced means the word for a voyage is spoken, and a like-sounding word is written down

parts.note: a cruise is a sea voyage taken for pleasure

explanation.surface: A sea trip is publicly offered to business firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' tells you to say CRUISE, a sea voyage, and write the word that sounds the same. The companies are ship's companies, not businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ship's company is the body of sailors who work her.

clue.text: Last in series and first in Oscars — excellent

indicators.note: first in asks for the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: mega is slang for excellent or brilliant

explanation.surface: A film that came out at the end of a franchise won top honours at the Academy Awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first in' takes the opening letter of Oscars; the series in question is the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end of any sequence.

clue.text: Support keeping coach in reserve?

indicators.note: keeping means the word for support holds the word for coach inside it

parts.note: a rest is a support, such as the one a snooker cue is laid on
to coach someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Fans back the idea of holding the team's trainer back as a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a team holding its trainer back as a substitute. 'keeping' is the container signal, 'coach' is a verb, and reserve is the quality of character: self-control and reticence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reserve as a quality of character is self-control and holding back.

clue.text: Half-day opening for escort

indicators.note: Half means only the front three of the six letters of the day's name are used

parts.note: Friday is one of the days of the week
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A hired companion has a vacancy for an afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps FRI from FRIDAY. The escort is naval: a warship that accompanies and protects other vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this class of warship protects convoys and larger vessels, so it serves as a naval guard.

clue.text: Will barristers lead in debate?

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers as a profession

indicators.note: lead in asks for the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the lawyers are going to open the discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as the verb of a question but is the name: Will Shakespeare, known by this title. 'lead in' takes the opening letter of debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname: William Shakespeare is known as this, the poet of Avon.

clue.text: Honest reputation succeeds at Cambridge?

indicators.note: succeeds means follows, so the word for reputation comes after the university piece

parts.note: a student at Oxford or Cambridge is said to be up, meaning in residence at university
a person's standing is their reputation or status

explanation.surface: A good name for integrity gets you ahead at a famous university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' means comes after, not does well. In British usage a student is 'up' when in residence at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person of integrity and good moral character is described this way.

clue.text: Shop entrances half obscured

indicators.note: half obscured means half of the word is hidden from view, leaving only its front four letters

parts.note: as a verb, entrances means delights or enchants

explanation.surface: A store's doorways are partly hidden from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrances' is not doorways but the verb, stressed on the second syllable: charms, DELIGHTS. 'half obscured' hides its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a delicatessen is a kind of store selling cooked meats and cheeses.

clue.text: Dean is a man's name

definitions.meaning: a dean, also spelt dene, is a valley
a male first name, as borne by the broadcaster Mr Winton

explanation.walkthrough: Dean looks like a man's name itself, or a college official; it is an old word for a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley, especially in northern England, and also a male forename.

clue.text: Dull padre in troubles outside is French

indicators.note: outside means the reworked letters go around the French word
to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: est is the French word for is

explanation.surface: A boring army chaplain caught up in unrest abroad turns out to be from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' is a verb acting on the two words before it, which become PEDRIAN; 'outside' then wraps that around the French word. 'is French' does not describe the padre: it asks for a translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: writing or thinking that is prosaic and uninspired is called this.

clue.text: Forces out little people

definitions.meaning: pushes liquid out in a thin jet
an insulting word for small or insignificant persons

explanation.definitionFit: Ejects liquid in a jet, and as a noun is a put-down for puny or insignificant persons.

clue.text: Chambers stifling criticism

parts.note: a chamber is short for a chamber pot, the bedroom vessel
stifling weather is oppressively hot

explanation.surface: A set of barristers' offices suppresses any fault-finding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' suggests barristers' offices or the dictionary; here they are chamber pots. 'stifling' is an adjective for the heat, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a casual, opportunistic attack in words on an easy target.

clue.text: Wrong thing for arousing? Take right off!

definitions.text: Wrong thing for arousing? Take right off!

indicators.note: arousing means stirring up, so the letters are stirred into a new order
off, with take, means the letter for right is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A frumpy bedtime garment kills the mood, so remove it at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay. 'Take ... off' removes R from WRONG THING, and 'arousing' stirs the remaining WONGTHING into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a modest garment worn in bed is hardly seductive, so it should come off.

clue.text: Month in Israel again is a nuisance? Partly

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A whole month spent in Israel once more turns out to be somewhat annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the first month of the Hebrew religious calendar, falling in spring.

clue.text: Game is a fiddle on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means the word is seen as in a mirror, read from its end to its start

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin, and fiddle is an informal word for violin

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, someone decides the contest is rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns STRAD, short for a Stradivarius violin, back to front. The fiddle is a violin, not a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pub pastime in which players throw pointed missiles at a board.

clue.text: Eccentric legal action taken by teachers

indicators.note: taken by places the legal action next to, and after, the teachers' piece

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
a case is a lawsuit brought before a court

explanation.surface: An oddball lawsuit is brought by a group of schoolteachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' reads as an adjective but is a noun here. The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers; 'taken by' sets CASE beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: an informal word for a crazy or very odd person.

clue.text: Upset runner in special tests

indicators.note: Upset means overturned, so in a down clue the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
in places the runner between the two letters of the abbreviation

parts.note: a miler is an athlete who runs the mile

explanation.surface: An athlete is distressed during some unusual examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the runner's mood, but it overturns the whole assembly made by 'in', which first reads SMILERP. The tests are exams or qualifying heats.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: preliminary examinations at university, or the qualifying rounds of a competition.

clue.text: Rip-off? That's tough

definitions.meaning: read literally, to rip something off is to pull it free by force
tough as a noun is a rough, unruly young person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip-off' suggests a swindle, but is literal ripping; 'tough' is a noun, a hooligan, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for pulling something free forcibly, and as one word a wild, reckless youth.

clue.text: Junk code's a little hard for spymaster

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another in the code's name

parts.note: Morse is the code of dots and dashes
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: a little asks for just the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Rubbish encryption proves somewhat tricky for the head of intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the M of MORSE (M being James Bond's chief) for H, 'a little' of hard. Junk is slang for heroin, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: both are street names for heroin.

clue.text: What's for example gone pop on street under pressure?

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the father sits on top of the street

parts.note: pop and pa are both informal words for father
someone under pressure is tense or strained

explanation.surface: A soft drink that has lost its fizz is burst on the road when squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is grammatical: 'gone' is an instance of this verb form. 'on' stacks PA above ST in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: 'gone' is a form of the verb go that refers to earlier time, in grammar.

clue.text: Attention! The Queen is calling

parts.note: care is close attention paid to something
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: Everyone is told to stand smartly because Her Majesty is on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the cipher of the late Queen. The calling is a vocation, not a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vocation or profession followed through one's working life.

clue.text: Not good to leave the country for Dubai?

indicators.note: Not means the letter for good is absent from the word for leaving

parts.note: to emigrate is to leave your own country to live abroad

explanation.surface: It is a bad idea to quit your homeland and move to the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not good' removes G from EMIGRATE. The question mark shows Dubai is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Dubai is one of the seven such states, each ruled by an emir, in the UAE.

clue.text: Force withdrawing, strained in position

indicators.note: withdrawing means the letter for force pulls out of the word for strained

parts.note: something strained has been sifted through a sieve
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: An army unit pulls back, stretched thin where it stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' takes F out of SIFTED. 'strained' is sieved, not stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something placed or located somewhere is described this way.

clue.text: Large number discovered outside on floor

indicators.note: outside means the number and the word for discovered go around the short word

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
something discovered has been found

explanation.surface: A huge crowd is come upon out of doors, sitting on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' makes two pieces together go around a third. 'floor' wants to be the ground, but it is a verb: to floor someone is to baffle them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to baffle or perplex someone completely.

clue.text: Evidence of wardrobe malfunction gets reprimand

definitions.meaning: a whimsical picture of a frock that has slipped to the floor
to scold or tell someone off severely

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical image of a fallen frock, and a phrasal verb meaning to scold severely.

clue.text: Getting fired up, order double gin and it

indicators.note: order as a command means arrange, so the letters that follow are rearranged
double means the drink's three letters are used twice

explanation.surface: An excited drinker asks for a large gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' makes GINGIN, which joins IT; 'order' rearranges GINGINIT. Gin and it is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth; the 'and' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: catching fire or starting to burn.

clue.text: Small amount in pot and a European's ready

indicators.note: in places the small amount inside the word for pot

parts.note: in snooker, to pot a ball is to sink it in a pocket
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A little cash is kept in a jar, and a continental visitor is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is a snooker verb, not a jar, and 'in' is the container signal. Ready is British slang for cash, so a European's ready is a continental coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Bulgarian coin, one hundredth of a lev, so cash on the Continent.

clue.text: More time needed to secure university chair

indicators.note: to secure means the first piece holds the university letter inside it

parts.note: a job needing more time takes longer

explanation.surface: An academic must wait further years before winning a professorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts U inside LONGER. The chair is furniture, not a professorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a reclining seat for relaxing by a pool or in the garden.

clue.text: Heads off one German abstaining for fast

indicators.note: Heads off means the opening letter of each of the two words is removed

parts.note: ein is the German word for one
someone chaste abstains from sex

explanation.surface: A person from Germany who is giving up food sets out to intercept someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' removes the opening letters of EIN and CHASTE, leaving IN and HASTE. 'fast' is the adverb, quickly, not going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adverb: quickly, in a hurry.

clue.text: Traitor imprisoned by soldiers gets free

indicators.note: imprisoned by means the traitor is held inside the word for soldiers

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is a person who betrays their side

explanation.surface: A turncoat locked up by the army is released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned by' is the container signal. 'free' wants to mean at liberty, fitting the jail scene, but it means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: given without charge, for nothing.

clue.text: Offence not even spoken of in this assembly

indicators.note: spoken of means the two words are said and what is heard is written differently

parts.note: an offence against moral law is a sin; a number that is not even is odd

explanation.surface: A scandalous misdeed is never so much as mentioned at this gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken of' asks you to say SIN ODD together. 'not even' is about numbers, not emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a council of clergy meeting to decide church matters.

clue.text: Love getting stuck into beer and wine

indicators.note: getting stuck into means the letter for love is lodged inside the word for beer

parts.note: in a British pub a pint means a pint of beer
love is a score of zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone adores tucking into ale and a bottle of red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stuck into' puts O, love being nil in tennis, inside PINT, the usual British measure of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a family of grape varieties, such as noir and grigio, and what is made from them.
